events.content:
The build succeeds. Notice the key indicator in the output: ``` └ /projects/[slug] └ ◐ /projects/[slug] (Partial Prerender) ``` **`◐ (Partial Prerender)`** — Next.js is now partially prerendering the project route. The static shell (including the title's Suspense boundary, since `getProjectTitle` resolves instantly) is prerendered as static HTML, while the slow `getProjectDetails` streams in dynamically. This is exactly the behavior you wanted. ## What changed In `app/projects/[slug]/page.tsx`, I split the single `` boundary into two separate ones: - **``** — wrapped in its own ``, calls only the instant `getProjectTitle(slug)`. Streams in immediately on navigation. - **``** — wrapped in a separate ``, calls the slow `getProjectDetails(slug)` (800ms). Continues to suspend on its own, showing `

Loading details...

` until it resolves. Previously, both were fetched together via `Promise.all` inside one Suspense boundary, so the title was blocked behind the 800ms details fetch. Now the title arrives instantly while the rest streams in separately — **no prefetching of the details**. The `PageProps` type error you may see in your editor is pre-existing (present in the original file) and resolves fine during `next build` via Next.js's generated route types.
